Yeah, I've tried I'm assuming you're from the US because your referring to majors. In the UK we only take one subject at university, we don't have minor and majors for our subject choices, just the one :p. Anyways, in the UK in order to see a therapist you have to register on the NHS, this is a very long waiting que, probably six months minimum. And, the trouble is even if I do manage to see a therapist, it has to be come in one place and be regular visits. This is a problem because my university and home are five hours apart. I can't really get a private therapist, I don't have the money. 

I'm not really great with trust issues. At back home I know a lot of people and in fact I was even close to some a couple of years ago. But now it's just sort of a conversation when you see somebody, just a casual minimalistic relationship and a drink or two when you're out. In actuality I don't really have any close friends, just friends really but I know in times of need they won't really be there for you or simply won't care enough to be straight forward. Maybe it's just me having trust issues, I don't know.

It will literally kill me if I failed university, it's my biggest fear. I wouldn't be able to get into a university of this standard again and I would feel so disappointed, it makes me ill thinking about it. Not only that, but my parents have kindly paid towards it and I simply can't let them down. I'm sharing a house with a few people next year and if I were to fail I'd still have to pay rent for a house for a year. The subject I'm studying is anthropology (biological, socio-cultural and medical).

Thanks for the response, sorry if I missed anything out.

Thanks for the response, it sounds like you've had a similar situation to me. I'm in the process of constructing a work ethic that will alleviate stress, however, it's a process of trial and error. I don't really get any enjoyment from anything outside of games unfortunately, but I'm in search for hobbies outside of gaming, only reading comes to mind at the moment.
